This note records observations, not a mathematical correctness grant. The whole exact task/family, augmented task, all actual nine FINAL fields, all expanded nine fields, entire native 58826-byte paper, entire 151629-byte standalone reader, whole qualified G331 paper/annotation/source ledger/scope, new candidate ledger/scope/coverage/decision, ROOT342 working proof and B341 source qualification data were read. The proof bodies were read as complete units; independent byte comparisons establish which redundant bodies are actually identical. The nine actual FINAL texts differ from their nine expanded texts. Counts refer only to the actual FINAL.

Fresh review_data.py reports 68/68 current size and SHA-256 matches: 30 mathematical files, five historical evidence files and 33 primary files. compare_packets.py independently checks every explicit historical author 15 own-file entry, all 54 input origins and all 54 author-local input copies; all match and none in these sets is unavailable. Supplied programs were read only as bytes for hashes, never executed/imported. Older unsupplied recursive histories are not represented as freshly checked. All nine expanded TeX proofs occur once in both candidate papers and equal the respective expanded native-note texts.

The independent reader reconstruction is exact: inline the four bound appendix bodies and replace both occurrences of the T1 font declaration with the three fontspec/DejaVu declarations. The first embedded G331 source is therefore NOT byte-identical; three other components are. Its mathematical body is unchanged. This precisely corrects the ROOT receipt's literal unchanged-body wording without modifying either immutable paper. The original grant copies supplied in qualified-G331/ remain byte-identical. The original task JSON problem exactly matches original-task-statement.txt modulo a final newline; the latter plus augmented-assignment.txt exactly reconstructs the author's augmented problem. The original completion criteria are preserved as a prefix.

Fresh six-page source rendering and visual inspection confirm SH 17.2.4 radical conditions, 17.4.3 factorial/ambient-degree convention, 17.4.6 finite annihilator, 17.4.7's INVALID unquotiented colon printing, and BFJ (4.3)/4.4's sign, generic colength and coefficient-topology argument. In k[[x,y]], the literal (x):y=(x) is infinite-length. The legitimate correction is ((x):y)/(x), equivalently the annihilator of y in R/(x), which is zero. The candidate's actual repeated-17.4.6 argument uses this current quotient; it does not require adopting the invalid printing. B341 supplied no theorem premise. Complete fresh source applications and the distinct recursive-history boundary are recorded in whole-source-application-ledger.md. All acquired source bodies and pixels remain local.

Fresh bounded_checks.py reports exactly 2060 checks, zero failures: 25 diagonal cases, 625 mixed-area, 625 moment-symmetry, 625 product-atom, 100 actual strict-maximum comparisons, 24 contraction minima and 36 residue first differences. Its explicit domain is axis exponents 1..5 (25 two-generator monomial ideals), all 625 ordered pairs, contraction N=1..24 with exponents in 0..2N, and residue d=2,3,5, r=1,2,4, N=1..4. The Newton formulas use exact rational gauges, primitive normals and integer polygon areas. These finite arithmetic observations do not prove their geometric interpretation or any arbitrary-ring theorem. The author's separately supplied 6765-check output was read as data and was not rerun or promoted to proof.

notes.summary: Independent all-field mixed-multiplicity kernel, retaining units, unused labels and nonpure/embedded superficial quotients.
notes.detailedSummary: Whole-form identities prove product/power laws and closure invariance. Simultaneous superficial elements in the same quotients prove monotonicity after exact R(z); stabilized finite colons and top-form additivity are reconstructed. Literal SH 17.4.7 is qualified.
notes.text:
## n2. Algebraic reconstruction

For a finite R-module M and proper primary labels I_1,...,I_r, use SH 17.4.2 at this Noetherian local ring: l(M/(prod I_j^s_j)M) is eventually a polynomial of degree dim M. Define its degree-n form H_M, with coefficients e(I_1^[d_1],...,I_r^[d_r];M)/(prod d_j!), |d|=n. This is the ambient-ring-degree convention of 17.4.3: H_M=0 if dim M<n. In n separately labeled slots e(I_1,...,I_n) is the coefficient of s_1...s_n. These definitions also apply on the possibly nonreduced auxiliary rings below, always using their current dimension. A unit variable is absent; any mixed coefficient using it is zero.

Unused variables are not removed by evaluating an eventual formula at exponent zero. Fix an unused B exponent at a large c. With another primary label K choose K^N subset B^c. For the remaining product P_s, P_s K^N subset B^c P_s subset P_s. Consequently the middle length is squeezed between two eventual polynomials whose degree-n forms are the same, since an exponent shift is constant. On each positive rational ray, after clearing its denominator, the difference divided by the ray parameter^n tends to zero. Thus the middle degree-n form is the form of the remaining labels. In the full polynomial the terms that retain degree n in the other variables have B exponent zero. Equality on all positive rational rays is polynomial identity, proving unused-label deletion. If every label is unused the positive-degree coefficient vanishes.

Permutation of variables proves symmetry. Replacing the variable for I by l times itself proves scaling by l for one mixed entry I^l. To split IJ introduce separate I,J variables and substitute both by one variable s. In the coefficient s s_2...s_n, the I,J degrees have sum one, so only (1,0) and (0,1) occur. Deleting their unused labels proves e(IJ,K_2,...,K_n)=e(I,K_2,...,K_n)+e(J,K_2,...,K_n). Iteration handles every product and power, including unit factors. Repeated equal labels are handled by replacing their separate variables by their sum in the polynomial for the merged label, which gives exactly the factorial convention.

Integral-closure invariance is equality, not coefficientwise order. If I subset J and J is integral over I, the finitely many generators of Jt satisfy homogeneous integral equations over R[It]. Hence R[Jt] is a finite graded module over R[It]. Homogeneous generators in degrees <=c imply J^(m+c) subset I^m for every m>=1. For m>c and any remaining product P_s,

    I^m P_s subset J^m P_s subset I^(m-c) P_s.

The outer length polynomials have the same highest form. The rational-ray squeeze proves equality of the middle highest form, hence equality of all mixed coefficients. Equal closures reduce to this twice through I+J; every generator of I+J is integral over either ideal. No implication from a nonnegative polynomial to coefficient order is used: (s-t)^2 already disproves such an implication.

For monotonicity compare J subset I with the SAME other labels K_2,...,K_n. When necessary set T=R[z]_(mR[z]). This local extension is faithfully flat, with residue k(z). A finite-length composition series tensors exactly to a composition series with residue factors k(z), preserving length, including all the length functions in use. Its dimension is n: a system of n parameters extends to an mT-primary ideal, giving dim T<=n by the height theorem, and flat going-down lifts an n-chain below mT, giving dim T>=n. Thus the polynomial coefficients do not change. There is no assertion about boundary extension to T.

Over the infinite residue field, SH 17.2.2 gives a complement of finitely many proper linear subspaces in K_n/mK_n for each compared family, with the selected label relabeled first. Intersect both complements and avoid the current minimal primes. This avoidance remains possible in nonpure quotients: if K_n subset P+mK_n, Nakayama on K_n/(K_n intersect P) would give K_n subset P, impossible for a primary ideal and a minimal P below the maximal ideal in positive dimension. Choose ONE x for BOTH families and quotient by it. If the current dimension is d>0, then dim R/(x)=d-1. Indeed any quotient chain can be extended strictly below its first prime to a minimal prime avoiding x, giving the upper bound; a parameter system of the quotient together with x gives the lower bound by height. No equidimensionality or CM assumption enters this step.

Here is the colon calculation explicitly. Write P_s=I_1^s_1...I_r^s_r with x in I_1. A submodule direct sum of intersections inside the finite module over R[I_1t_1,...,I_rt_r] is finitely generated. Taking maximum generator multidegrees yields multi-ideal Artin--Rees, SH 17.1.6. Applying it to xR intersect P_s gives

    (P_s:x) subset (0:x)+P_(s-e)

for one fixed multivector e and large s. Because all radicals are m, some I_1^h is contained in I_1^c prod_(j>1) I_j^e_j. Hence for large s the remainder P_(s-e) lies in I_1^c prod_(j>1) I_j^s_j, the truncated superficial range. Intersecting with the colon there and using superficiality gives

    (P_s:x)=(0:x)+P_(s-e_1).

For large fixed other exponents, (0:x) intersect P_(s-e_1) is zero: an element in the annihilator and the truncated range lies, by superficiality at every arbitrarily large first exponent, in I_1^N R for all N; Krull intersection makes it zero. This is the radical and separation content of SH 17.2.4, not a regular-element claim. Thus (0:x) injects into a finite primary quotient and has finite length. Multiplication by x in the four-term exact sequence yields

    l(R/P_s)-l(R/P_(s-e_1))
       =l(R/(x,P_s))-l(0:x).

For d>1 the annihilator is a constant term, so comparing degree d-1 gives exactly SH 17.4.6. Choose the selected K_n exponent one in the mixed coefficient; its removal gives the mixed coefficient in R/(x), with the unused K_n variable deleted by the preceding argument. Repeat in K_(n-1),...,K_2, using simultaneous choices in each common quotient. Primary images stay proper primary. Embedded primes and nilpotents are allowed. The final one-dimensional ring R' gives e_R'(JR') and e_R'(IR'); inclusion of their powers and the one-variable length leading coefficients give e_R'(JR')>=e_R'(IR'). This proves every-slot mixed monotonicity by symmetry, and positivity for all proper entries by the positive one-dimensional Samuel leading coefficient. For n=1 the last argument is direct; units yield zero. Combined with closure invariance this also gives monotonicity for closure inclusions.

For a short exact sequence M_1 -> M_2 -> M_3, use multi-ideal Artin--Rees on P_s M_2 intersect M_1. It lies between P_s M_1 and P_(s-c) M_1. Their length highest forms agree by the same ray squeeze. The exact sequence of the actual induced quotients, rather than a false injection modulo P_s, now gives H_M2=H_M1+H_M3. This reconstructs SH 17.4.4 and gives zero contribution for modules of dimension below n.

G331's primary valuative criterion applies on ALL X: v(J)>=v(K) iff J subset bar(K). A positive-dimensional local reduced R has no zero-dimensional minimal component, so the extra zero-image condition in its componentwise criterion is vacuous here. A unit comparison is direct. Equal rational profiles -v(I)/q=-v(I')/q' give equal closures of I^q' and (I')^q. The proved power laws give identical mixed inputs. Profile inequalities give the correct reversed order of positive ideal moments. This criterion is used on R, not on an unexamined quotient boundary.

SH 17.4.7's literal colon length is NOT used. At the final step it must mean

    l(0 :_(M/(x_1,...,x_(d-1))M) x_d)
      =l(((x_1,...,x_(d-1))M :_M x_d)/(x_1,...,x_(d-1))M).

The unquotiented printed module can have infinite length: in k[[x,y]], (x):y=(x). Our source pixels on PDF 370, printed 356, show the omitted quotient in the literal printing. Repeated 17.4.6 above supplies the finite valid correction.

notes.summary: Positive all-support bounded moment measures with full representation independence and actual prescribed-limit decreasing-NET continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves test relations, positive real Riesz extension, mass and binomial perturbation bounds, C and bounded D extension, exact majorant supremum, additivity and every uniform/decreasing-net limit inside the stated domain. No increasing closure or measure order.
notes.text:
## n3. Positive moment measures and all bounded nets

For rational inputs u_i=-v(I_i)/q_i, i=1,...,p, define B_u(v(J))=e(I_1,...,I_p,J)/prod q_i. At p=0 the denominator is one and this is e(J). Extend to rational ideal differences. Every rational linear combination of gauges is representable as (v(J)-v(K))/d, by synchronized denominators and products, with unit-or-primary J,K. If two such representations agree, then v(J^d' (K')^d)=v(K^d' (J')^d) everywhere. Proper products have equal integral closures by n2; equality with a unit forces both products to be units. Their mixed moment laws prove equality of the proposed values. Nonnegativity of a difference gives inclusion in the closure of the opposite ideal and thus functional positivity by mixed monotonicity. This proves test relation independence on every support, as well as input independence.

Since 1=v(a), positivity on r+f and r-f for rational r>||f|| gives |B(f)|<=||f|| B(1). G331's separating rational lattice is uniformly dense in the REAL C(X); no irrational ideal expression is needed. Its continuous extension is real-linear by rational scalar limits and positive: approximate h>=0 by f_j in the lattice and use f_j+r_j>=0, with rational r_j>||h-f_j|| tending to zero. Compact-Hausdorff Riesz gives the unique finite positive Radon measure mu_u with mass B(1)=e(I_1,...,I_p,a)/prod q_i. This uses neither metrizability nor measure order.

Write E_J=e(a^[p],J). If every input is in [-M,0], comparison with -M=-M v(a) gives

    0<=B_u(v(J))<=M^p E_J,
    mu_u(X)<=M^p e(a).

Real M is obtained by decreasing rational upper bounds. For two tuples in this range, ||u_i-w_i||<=epsilon gives u_i-epsilon<=w_i and conversely. The legitimate negative shift is an input in the same cone. Multilinearity expands its moment into the unshifted term and one term for every nonempty subset of shifted slots. A subset of size r contributes <=epsilon^r M^(p-r) E_J. Therefore

    |B_u(v(J))-B_w(v(J))|
      <=Delta_p(M,epsilon) E_J,
    Delta_p(M,epsilon)=(M+epsilon)^p-M^p.                 (U)

Use rational upper errors when coefficients are initially rational; Delta_0=0 and M^0=1, including M=0.

Approximate any C tuple uniformly by rational profiles. One common bound makes all ideal moments Cauchy by (U). Their limits define a positive bounded lattice functional and hence a measure. Different approximations give the same limits. Symmetry, addition and real nonnegative homogeneity pass from rational tuples. If u<=w, approximation errors eta give u_app-2eta<=w_app; (U) removes the shift and proves moment order. Thus all these laws and (U) hold on C. For any continuous test, first approximate by the dense lattice and bound the two residual integrals by its sup error times the common mass bound. Consequently moment convergence implies weak convergence, also for uniformly convergent nets.

For bounded u_i in D take ANY actual decreasing C representations g_(i,alpha_i) down to u_i. Since g>=u>=-M and g<=0, they already lie in [-M,0]. On the finite product directed set the ideal moments increase and have a finite supremum. Differences of their limits define the positive bounded lattice functional: each defining approximant is positive on nonnegative lattice tests and has the common norm bound. Riesz and the preceding density estimate give the measure and weak convergence.

Compare another representation f_beta. For fixed beta and epsilon>0 the continuous strict open sets {g_(i,alpha)<f_(i,beta)+epsilon} form directed covers of compact X. Select one alpha for each slot valid everywhere. Moment order and (U) give

    B_fbeta(v(J))<=B_(g_alpha-epsilon)(v(J))
      <=sup_alpha B_galpha(v(J))+Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J.

Send epsilon to zero, then take sup_beta, and interchange representations. This proves full representation independence. Applying the same cover argument to any C majorant h>=u, and observing that the representing terms themselves are majorants, gives the exact formula

    B_u(v(J))=sup { B_h(v(J)): h_i in C, h_i>=u_i }.      (M)

All these majorants are in [-M,0]. The majorant set for a larger tuple is smaller, proving ideal-moment order on bounded D. This is not an order of measures: nonnegative ideal tests do not exhaust all nonnegative continuous tests for comparisons between measures.

Addition uses actual finite product representations: g_alpha+f_beta decreases to u+w, with known D membership from G331, and at each index C additivity holds. Bounded scalar limits prove additivity, symmetry and nonnegative real scaling on D. Zero scaling is the actual zero function. Consequently the negative shift expansion and (U) hold on the entire established bounded D domain. Uniform convergence inside this domain, with its eventual common bound, gives weak convergence by the lattice and mass argument. No increasing-limit membership is asserted.

Finally let u_(i,lambda) decrease in bounded D with common [-M,0] bound to a SPECIFIED u_i in D. Moment order bounds sup_lambda B_u_lambda by B_u. Fix a C majorant tuple h and epsilon>0. The sets {u_(i,lambda)<h_i+epsilon} are open because D functions are upper semicontinuous; they are increasing directed covers since their pointwise limits are <=h_i. Compactness selects one common lambda. Thus

    B_h(v(J))<=B_(u_lambda-epsilon)(v(J))
      <=B_u_lambda(v(J))+Delta_p(M,epsilon)E_J.

Taking sup_lambda, sending epsilon to zero, and taking the majorant supremum (M) proves exact target moment convergence. Common mass and lattice density give weak convergence for every continuous test. Limit membership is essential to this statement; neither arbitrary-infimum closure nor nested-net flattening was used. The entire construction is uniquely forced by the rational moments and these two continuities.

notes.summary: Independent supported Cartier degree with all nilpotent layers, actual Koszul symmetry, cycle projection and raw Rees comparison.
notes.detailedSummary: m-filtration handles mixed characteristic. Supported complexes allow improper intersections. Nonpure top-component and one-dimensional cycle decomposition precede proper projection. Eventual Rees H0/Serre vanishing and polynomial identity prove the mixed comparison; DVR local degree remains one.
notes.text:
## n4. Independently supported Cartier intersection Let Y=Bl_I Spec R be an actual primary model. G331 gives its reduced dominating components, regular effective E_I, ample O(-E_I), directed refinements and actual exceptional Cartier order unit. For an effective exceptional integral Cartier E, a power of m kills O_E. Indeed its coherent support is in the closed fibre; on a finite affine cover the radical containment becomes a common power containment. E is proper over the resulting Artinian quotient of R. Its coherent cohomology is finite over R by 0B5S and killed by that power; higher cohomology is bounded in degree on a finite affine cover. Define chi_R(E,F)=sum_j (-1)^j l_R H^j(E,F). The dimension bound needed here is dim E<=p, also for nonpure R. On a component dominating R/P, the catenary finite-type dimension function delta(x)=dim(R/image(x))+trdeg of residue fields has generic value dim R/P. A point over m has delta equal to its residue transcendence degree, and a proper closed exceptional subset has delta-dimension at most dim R/P-1. Thus each closed-fibre component has ordinary k-dimension at most p. This also shows why smaller dominating components cannot supply a dimension-p exceptional component. Do not apply a field Euler lemma directly to E in mixed characteristic. Filter O_E by m^j O_E. Every graded quotient G_j is coherent on the proper k-scheme E_0 and has support dimension <=p. Tensoring by any line bundle is exact. Euler additivity, equality of R-length and k-dimension for the quotient cohomologies, and complete Stacks 0BEL 33.45.1 show that P_E(t)=chi_R(E,O_E tensor prod O(F_i)^t_i) is a polynomial of total degree <=p, for all integer twists. Define Q_Y(F_1,...,F_p,E) as its coefficient t_1...t_p. When p=0 this is l_R H^0(E,O_E); a proper zero-dimensional scheme over an Artinian base is finite and has no higher cohomology. The definition includes every nilpotent layer of E. Apply 33.45.2 to each G_j. At a dimension-p generic point eta_Z, the local lengths add to l_(O_Y,eta_Z)(O_E,eta_Z). The m-quotient local ring has the same residue field; the finite modules killed by m have the same composition length over both local rings. Lower-dimensional supports have degree O_E1(-E_2) -> O_(E_1+E_2) -> O_E2 -> 0 and fixed-twist invariance prove additivity of the effective last slot. G331's order unit expresses any integral exceptional F as (F+NE_I)-NE_I with both effective. Equality of two such differences is equality of effective sums, so extension is independent of decomposition. Then extend over the real Cartier tensor group by multilinearity. Full symmetry requires a supported calculation even for improper intersections. For effective E,F take their ACTUAL two-term locally free resolutions K_E=[O(-E)->O], K_F=[O(-F)->O]. Their tensor products, with a line bundle L, are canonically the same total Koszul complex up to interchange signs. To compute its Euler characteristic, resolve first E and then F, or conversely: the resulting complexes [O_E tensor L(-F)->O_E tensor L] and [O_F tensor L(-E)->O_F tensor L] have finite-length cohomology in every term. The free terms on Y individually need NOT have finite length; no alternating length of those free terms is taken. Their hypercohomology Euler identities give chi_R(E,L)-chi_R(E,L(-F)) =chi_R(F,L)-chi_R(F,L(-E)). (K) The complexes remain valid if either induced cut is improper or a zerodivisor. Let L=O(F)^t O(E)^s prod_(j=1)^(n-2) O(G_j)^r_j, set t=s=0 in (K), and read r_1...r_(n-2). The left finite difference is the coefficient t r_1...r_(n-2): a higher power of t would exceed the total-degree bound p. The right is the corresponding s coefficient. Therefore Q(F,G_1,...,G_(n-2),E)=Q(E,G_1,...,G_(n-2),F). Effective differences and real linearity give all transpositions. There is no exchange to prove at n=1. This local degree is not a degree homomorphism on global CH_0(Y). For the DVR Y=Spec k[[t]], Q((t))=1 while [(t)] is the principal, hence zero, Chow class. Our definition works on the proper supported thickening and retains the one. For proper primary refinements and finite normalizations use Spec R with delta(P)=dim R/P. Local catenarity gives the unit drops across immediate specializations; excellence supplies universal catenarity for Stacks 02QL. Extend delta to finite type models by residue transcendence degrees. Each top component has delta-dimension n. The pullback of an exceptional Cartier equation is regular: on every reduced dominating component it is nonzero at the generic point; regularity follows by injection into the product of component domains. Smaller components have exceptional fibre dimension <=dim R/P-1

direct sum_(minimal P) B/P has a finite-length cokernel T, since it is an isomorphism at the minimal primes. Multiplication by a regular equation g and the kernel/cokernel sequence, with l(T[g])=l(T/gT), give l(B/gB)=sum_P l((B/P)/g(B/P)). Thus the top divisor cycle equals the sum of divisor cycles on the integral top components, whose generic weights are one. On each such component Stacks 0AYA 42.26.3 applies to the proper dominant map, equal delta-dimension, and the pulled-back Cartier meromorphic section. The function-field degree is one. BEFORE any Chow quotient this proves f_*[f^*E]_p=[E]_p. (P) Apply 0BEL 33.45.7 to the proper k-schemes consisting of each closed-fibre prime and its image. This formula includes residue degrees and gives zero if the image dimension is O(qD_I) -> O((q-1)D_I) -> O_EI((q-1)D_I) -> 0 gives l_R(I^(q-1)/I^q)=chi_R(E_I,O_EI((q-1)D_I)). Its degree-p coefficient on the left is e(I)/p!, and on the right is Q(D_I^[p],E_I)/p!, by substituting the sum of p separately labeled variables. Thus Q(D_I^[p],E_I)=e(I), or -Q(D_I^[n])=e(I), including p=0. For I_1,...,I_n use a common product blowup. The product prod I_j^t_j has negative divisor sum t_j D_Ij. Formula (PI) permits its diagonal identity on that model. If H(t) is the degree-n multigraded length form, the product's Samuel multiplicity is n!H(t), by replacing all exponents with qt_j. Hence -Q((sum t_j D_Ij)^[n])=n!H(t) for every positive integral t. Equality on this grid is polynomial identity. Its t_1...t_n coefficients give -Q(D_I1,...,D_In)=e(I_1,...,I_n). (I) Units give zero slots. No normality, Cohen--Macaulayness, infinite residue field, or parameter-colength formula was used in this geometry.

notes.summary: Independent positive REAL nef atoms and refinement invariance, followed by a fixed-model real-core comparison.
notes.detailedSummary: Normal lifts, same-field DVR equality and exactly-one-prime projection prove atomic invariance first. One primary c0 and one Bl_(I c0) give the actual invertible IMAGE equality and maps to all Bl_Jq. Finite coefficient polynomials and all-support uniform profiles establish function/model independence.
notes.text:
## n5. Independent atomic geometry, invariance and real comparison

Normalize a common primary model Y. Excellence makes N->Y finite. Retain the top normal components for degree n; every other component and boundary point remains in the domain. Let Z range over the finitely many dimension-p exceptional prime divisors. Their generic local rings are DVRs. Put b_Z=ord_Z(a)>0 and nu_Z=ord_Z/b_Z, pulled back to R from its minimal component fraction field. For actual negative-effective real curve-nef D_1,...,D_p define, BEFORE identifying algebraic measures,

    mu_geom,Y=sum_Z b_Z (D_1|Z ... D_p|Z . Z) delta_nu_Z.  (A)

For p=0 the numerical coefficient is deg_k Z=[kappa(Z):k]. There is no generic residue factor omitted from this coefficient.

Positivity uses precisely qualified G331. On Y, subtract a small positive multiple of E_I from D_i. This is real ample by its proved real nef-plus-ample argument. Round all nonnegative effective-presentation coefficients upward to rational numbers, sufficiently little that finite-span openness preserves ampleness. G331's finite-Picard-subgroup rationalization makes the result genuinely Q-ample. These negative rational ample divisors L_ij converge in the finite coefficient spans to D_i. Finite normalization pulls their ample bundles to ample bundles, and restriction to each proper Z is ample. Clear denominators and use 33.45.9 for positive mixed intersections. Intersections are finite multilinear coefficient polynomials, so their limits are nonnegative. This establishes positivity of (A) independently of ideal positivity.

At nu_Z evaluation gives H_F(nu_Z)=ord_Z(F)/b_Z for every exceptional real Cartier F. Formula (C) on the normal model has DVR multiplicities ord_Z(F) for effective F; extend by differences. With (PI) this gives the independent geometric identity

    integral H_F dmu_geom,Y=Q_Y(D_1,...,D_p,F).             (G)

Independence of refinement is proved now, BEFORE algebraic moment comparison. If Y'->Y is a primary refinement, its normalization N' maps to N on each component: an integral function over the target chart is in every normal source local ring in the same fraction field. These local lifts agree generically and hence glue. The graph in N' x_Y N is closed since N is separated over Y; projection to N is proper because N'->Y is proper. The lift is birational on top components.

If an exceptional Z' maps dominantly to a dimension-p Z in N, the source DVR dominates the target DVR in the SAME fraction field. They are equal. For every field element write x=t^m u in the target DVR, with u a unit. Both u and u^-1 remain units upstairs and t is a nonunit there. Thus its sign of order is precisely the sign of m, proving equality of valuation rings, normalized orders and residue fields. Apply the ACTUAL cycle equality (P) to E_I, whose coefficient at every target exceptional Z is positive. Each dominant Z' then has the same positive coefficient and degree one, so (P) forces EXACTLY ONE such Z' over Z. Numerical projection gives its mixed intersection equal to the old mixed weight. Any remaining Z' has image dimension <p; its p pulled-back line bundles have zero intersection by 33.45.7. Consequently (A) is unchanged as a measure on X. This works componentwise, for common refinements and auxiliary normal lifts. In particular (G) can be tested on a common refinement for a test not originally determined on Y.

The bridge needs an actual sheaf identity. Fix Y=Bl_I R. From G331, T=H^0(Y,O_Y) is finite birational and T/R has closed-point support. Fix h with m^h(T/R)=0 and c_0=m^(h+1); then c_0 T subset m AS ELEMENTS OF R. For a negative rational ample exceptional L and large divisible q, O(qL) is globally generated. Its finite module of sections F_q lies in T. Put J_q=c_0 F_q. It is an ideal of R and is proper by c_0 T subset m. Away from m, section localization, the identity model and the divisor trivialization give J_q R_P=R_P. Hence J_q is proper primary, and contains a power of m.

Use ONE refinement Y'=Bl_(I c_0) R. Its product-ideal universal property makes the images of I and c_0 invertible; it maps to Y and Bl_c0 R. Let D_0 be the pulled-back negative divisor of c_0. Global generation gives a surjection F_q tensor O_Y -> O_Y(qL) whose IMAGE in O_Y is exactly that invertible ideal. Pullback preserves the surjection. The pulled-back ideal inclusion stays injective: its Cartier generator is nonzero on every reduced dominating component, hence regular. Multiply by the invertible regular image of c_0. Thus as actual image ideals in O_Y',

    J_q O_Y'=O_Y'(q f^*L+D_0).                            (S)

Its regular invertibility gives Y'->Bl_Jq R by 31.33.5. This is not merely equality of valuations, and the same c_0,Y' works for every divisor and approximation exponent.

For simultaneous negative rational ample L_1,...,L_n, with generated divisible q_i, use (I), (PI), and (S):

    e(J_(1,q_1),...,J_(n,q_n))/prod q_i
       =-Q_Y'(f^*L_1+D_0/q_1,...,f^*L_n+D_0/q_n).        (S2)

On EVERY support the equality of image ideals at the valued center also gives

    -v(J_q)/q=H_L-v(c_0)/q.                              (S3)

G331's all-support evaluation avoids using the total fraction ring at a nonminimal support: pull the invertible ideal and its generic trivialization to the support quotient valuation ring. A generating section has a unit coefficient there. Because c_0 is PRIMARY, v(c_0) has a uniform finite bound. Hence (S3) is uniform convergence.

Now approximate real core D_i by the negative rational ample L_ij above on the FIXED model; choose generated divisible q_ij tending to infinity. The same Y',D_0 applies. The right side of (S2) converges by its finite coefficient polynomial, independently of function convergence. The profiles in (S3) converge uniformly. The moment continuity of n3 and its common mass bound also allow the last test to vary uniformly: the error integral is at most the test's sup error times that mass. Since the test -v(J_(n,q_n))/q_n has negative moment -e/prod q_i, this proves

    integral H_Dn dmu_alg(H_D1,...,H_Dp)
       =Q_Y(D_1,...,D_p,D_n).                            (B)

No implication from uniform functions to intersection convergence was assumed.

For an arbitrary integral exceptional F choose N large enough that F-NE_I and -NE_I are both actual negative and ample, using G331's order unit and ample twisting. They are admissible core tests and their difference is F. Test linearity extends (B) to F, then to every real exceptional test. To test a primary ideal not determined on Y, go to a common primary refinement. The INDEPENDENT atomic invariance above, (G), and (B) identify all primary moments there. The dense ideal-difference lattice and finite mass give

    mu_geom,Y(D_1,...,D_p)
       =mu_alg(H_D1,...,H_Dp).                           (COMPARE)

Thus the geometric measure depends only on the functions, is independent of their presentations and primary models, and has the exact supported Cartier pairing on any common refinement. N3 extends this independently constructed geometric core to the full bounded geometric D. This supplies the required extra comparison theorem rather than merely renaming an ideal completion.

notes.text:
## n6. Strict maximum and bounded open locality

Suppose p>=1. For rational selected profiles synchronize denominators by powers: u=-v(A)/q, w=-v(B)/q; their maximum is -v(A+B)/q. Choose a common primary product model making A,B,A+B, every other input and a reference primary ideal invertible, then normalize. The reference factor handles all-unit cases. Unit divisors are zero and cause no change in the argument.

Set S=(A+B)O_N. Define the ACTUAL invertible subideals L=AO_N/S and M=BO_N/S in O_N. They satisfy L+M=O_N. If u(nu_Z)>w(nu_Z), then ord_Z(A)<ord_Z(B), hence ord_Z(M)>0. The map M|Z -> O_Z is zero: on any trivializing open its regular generator is zero at the generic point of integral reduced Z, and a regular section on this integral scheme that vanishes generically vanishes identically. Restrict L+M=O_N to Z. With M's map zero, L|Z surjects onto O_Z, so it is isomorphic to O_Z as a line bundle. Therefore the difference D_A-D_(A+B) restricts trivially to Z. Every mixed weight of (A) at an atom in the strict set is identical for u and max(u,w), with all other slots fixed. Both measures are on the same finite divisorial set, giving

    mu(max(u,w),others)|{u>w}=mu(u,others)|{u>w}.          (MAX)

This is an equality of geometric atomic weights, not an inference from moment order.

For C selected and other slots, take uniform rational approximants. A continuous test h with compact support K inside the open strict set has a positive minimum of u-w on K. Accurate approximants keep that strict gap throughout K. Their (MAX) identities and uniform weak continuity give equality of integrals against the FIXED h. Such tests determine Radon restrictions. Next hold selected u,w in C fixed and represent all other bounded D slots by actual decreasing C nets. The open set and h remain fixed; n3's prescribed-limit decreasing continuity extends (MAX) to those other slots.

For arbitrary bounded u,w in D agreeing on open U, fix the other bounded D slots and a continuous h with compact support K subset U. Take actual decreasing C representations u_alpha down to u and w_beta down to w; all terms have a common bound. Fix alpha and epsilon>0. The continuous open sets {w_beta-epsilon<u_alpha} form a directed cover of K, because their pointwise limits there satisfy w-epsilon=u-epsilon<u_alpha. Compactness selects beta_0; the strict open neighborhood of K at that index is fixed for this alpha,epsilon and remains valid for every later beta. The already proved selected-C identity yields

    integral h dmu(max(u_alpha,w_beta-epsilon),others)
       =integral h dmu(u_alpha,others).

First decrease beta. The known limit max(u_alpha,w-epsilon) belongs to bounded D by G331's finite-max stability (also by this actual representation). Apply n3's decreasing-net continuity. Then decrease alpha; the prescribed limit max(u,w-epsilon) is again in bounded D. A second application yields

    integral h dmu(max(u,w-epsilon),others)
       =integral h dmu(u,others).                        (L1)

These are two successive limits with fixed h, not flattening of nested D representations. Interchange u,w for a second identity. Both shifted maxima are uniformly within epsilon of the ALREADY KNOWN bounded D function max(u,w). Their possible increase as epsilon tends to zero is immaterial: use (U) inside this known domain and then weak convergence. The two right sides of (L1) have the same limiting integral, so mu(u,others) and mu(w,others) agree on all continuous tests supported compactly in U.

For completeness these tests determine the restrictions on U. For compact K subset U, compact Hausdorff normality gives a continuous cutoff equal to one on K whose support is contained in U (first shrink to an open set with closure in U). For positive Radon measures, inner regularity makes mass of an open subset of U the supremum of integrals of such cutoffs bounded by one. Hence equality of the test functionals gives equality on open subsets of U, and then on its Borel sets by Radon regularity. Replace input slots one at a time to prove full mixed locality. At p=0 locality is automatic. This is ordinary open locality on the entire compact normalized boundary; no plurifine or arbitrary Borel cutoff claim is made.

notes.text:
## n7. Gauge, normalization, curves and degeneracies

For another proper primary b let d(v)=v_a(b)>0 and T(v)=v/d(v). G331 supplies a homeomorphism and continuous bounded d,d^-1. Transport inputs by u_b(Tv)=u_a(v)/d(v). Rational profiles retain the same ideals and denominators, and v_b(J)(Tv)=v_a(J)/d. Thus testing T_*[d mu_a] against v_b(J) gives exactly the gauge-b mixed moment. Density proves

    mu_b=T_*[d mu_a].                                    (GAUGE)

There is ONE d factor independent of n, since it cancels the test's homogeneous denominator, rather than a count of input factors. The transported C and bounded decreasing D representations preserve uniform or pointwise decreasing convergence, so both proved continuities extend (GAUGE). Multiplication by fixed d and compact pushforward are weakly continuous. The new mass is the old moment against v_a(b), rationally e(I_1,...,I_p,b)/prod q_i. Along a third gauge, d_ab(v) d_bc(T_ab v)=v_a(c), proving the exact cocycle. On a geometric atom, b_Z changes from ord_Z(a) to ord_Z(b)=d(nu_Z)b_Z and its normalized point changes by T, giving the same rule directly.

Let S be the finite normalization of R and q its local normal centers over m. A regular conductor element kills S/R. For any prime in that module's support, a chain to m extends strictly below it to a minimal prime avoiding that regular element. Thus dim(S/R)<n. The top-form exact-sequence additivity of n2 gives H_R=H_S. For each primary product P, Artinian decomposition and composition series give

    l_R(S/PS)=sum_q f_q l_(S_q)(S_q/PS_q),
    f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)].

These are field-vector-space dimensions, with no separability assumption. Comparing degree-n forms yields

    e_R(I_1,...,I_n)
      =sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q e_(S_q)(I_1 S_q,...,I_n S_q).

When dim S_q<n its degree-n form is zero; it is not replaced by its own lower-dimensional intrinsic operator. Test on the lattice, then use uniform C and prescribed bounded decreasing D continuity, and obtain

    mu_R,a(u)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q rho_(q,*)
                  mu_(S_q,aS_q)(rho_q^*u).              (NORMAL)

All lower-dimensional centers, their boundary points, and every support remain in the space and potential domain. This is zero top-degree contribution, not point deletion.

For full-fiber-constant compatible upstairs C or D tuples, G331 grants actual positive descent. Its normalization quotient is unchanged: finite conductor value gives singleton fibres, and infinite conductor value gives exactly the equality of restrictions through S/c -> R/c. Apply (NORMAL) to their descended inputs, using the FULL maps rho_q. Identified fibres have their masses added under pushforward; no choice of representative is made. The same formula is now geometric by (COMPARE). This does not construct the entire arbitrary-finite-map operator calculus of P12.6.

For an excellent reduced curve n=1, normal local centers are DVRs. Their centered real semivaluations have zero support and are multiples of order, since every nonzero element is a parameter power times a unit. The regular conductor element has finite value on every branch. G331's singleton fibres therefore give the finite branch set nu_q=ord_q/b_q, b_q=ord_q(a)>0. The independent zero-input reference measure is

    mu_R,a()=sum_q f_q b_q delta_nu_q,
    mu_R,a(X)=e_R(a).                                   (CURVE)

Branches mean normalization LOCAL centers, including two branches on one irreducible nodal component. To verify actual Cartier degree on EVERY curve primary model Y, IS is invertible, so Spec S -> Y exists. Its graph in Spec S x_R Y proves it finite; the finite image contains all component generic points of reduced Y and hence is surjective. It is birational and normal, thus is Y's finite normalization. At a closed point y take B=O_Y,y, its finite semilocal normalization Btilde, and finite-length C=Btilde/B. For a regular Cartier equation g the snake exact sequence is

    0 -> C[g] -> B/gB -> Btilde/gBtilde -> C/gC -> 0.

The two end modules have equal lengths. Hence the local supported Cartier length equals the sum of the DVR orders with closed residue degrees, first over kappa(y) and then multiplied by [kappa(y):k]. Summing y and extending by effective differences and REAL coefficients gives Q_Y(F)=sum_q f_q ord_q(F)=integral H_F dmu(). This preserves local degree even when the global Chow class vanishes. DVR lengths also give the ideal moment e_R(J). Zero-arity continuity and locality are constant identities.

Residue degrees must not be replaced by generic degrees. For any finite k subset l of degree d>1, including purely inseparable extensions, set R=k+t l[[t]], S=l[[t]]. With k-basis 1,alpha_2,...,alpha_d, R=k[[t]] plus direct sum_(i>1) t k[[t]] alpha_i is a finite algebra over the excellent DVR k[[t]], hence excellent Noetherian. It is local with m=tS, residue k, fraction field l((t)), normalization S, conductor tS, generic degree one, residue degree d. For J=t^r S,

    l_R(R/J^N)=1+d(rN-1), e_R(J)=dr.

Its m-reference measure is d delta_ord_t, with moment dr. The calculation uses vector dimensions only and is valid for inseparable l/k.

If n=0, R is a field, X is empty and its measure is zero; there is no negative arity and no degree-zero multiplicity mass on an empty boundary. For n>=2 a zero input, represented by a unit, annihilates the product; a unit test has zero moment. At p=0 there is no input zero to annihilate the reference measure. Inputs -t_i v(a) have mass (prod t_i)e_R(a), with empty product one. The zero ideal has infinite value, its negative profile is unbounded bottom, and it is excluded from bounded inputs and primary gauges. Unit and zero ideals have no level-one section. Zero scaling is the actual zero function, never the undefined expression zero times infinity.

For nonreduced germs this is the reduction convention, not a hidden nilpotent intersection assertion. k[[t]][epsilon]/epsilon^2 and k[[t]] have identical semivaluation boundaries but parameter-power lengths 2s and s. Generic nilpotent lengths require extra reference data. In contrast, nilpotent thicknesses of exceptional Cartier divisors on reduced models are intrinsic to our supported construction and were fully retained in (C).

## n8. Exact smooth BFJ operator and arbitrary nets

Use BFJ only at a smooth CLOSED point of an affine variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, n>=2, initially in the maximal-ideal gauge. Its published Setting and full Section 4, including proofs, were read. G331 grants the full cone comparison on all semivaluations, with identically bottom adjoined; bottom is not a bounded input. No multiplier theorem is transferred to a singular or positive-characteristic ring.

BFJ (4.3) uses generic parameter colength. It equals our polynomial mixed multiplicity in this regular local ring. Consecutive superficial choices in SH 17.2.2 and the proof of 17.3.1 construct a joint-reduction parameter tuple for n primary ideals over the infinite field. The generic condition is genuinely open: for fixed diagonal degree N the map from the sum of the products missing each selected ideal to P_N/mP_N, multiplied by the selected coefficients, is a finite-dimensional linear-coefficient matrix. Full rank is an open minors condition, and Nakayama lifts it to the required ideal equality. A known joint reduction realizes it for some N, making this open set nonempty; the union over N describes all joint reductions. They are parameter tuples: the product ideal is integral over their joint-reduction ideal, so its radical is m and the generated n-element ideal has radical m. Complete SH 17.4.9 gives parameter multiplicity equal to the polynomial mixed coefficient. In a regular CM ring any parameter tuple is a regular sequence, whose multiplicity is its quotient length. Equivalently, repeated 17.4.6 along a superficial regular sequence has zero CURRENT-QUOTIENT annihilator. The invalid literal unquotiented 17.4.7 formula is unnecessary. Thus BFJ's generic colength equals our mixed coefficient.

The sign and arity are exact: BFJ pairs n negative ideal divisors with negative intersection, and (4.7) says the positive ideal test -log|J|=v(J) integrates to e(I_1,...,I_p,J). Real scaling and the unit/zero conventions therefore identify rational-profile measures by the dense lattice and finite mass. For C tuples, BFJ 4.4's addition and coefficient order give our same shift bound (U); mass is <=M^p e(m). Uniform rational approximation proves equality of C measures.

For bounded D tuples choose any actual decreasing C representation. At each divisorial prime its coefficient decreases to that of the G331-identified limit; hence this is convergence in the coefficient topology of nef Weil divisors. We need the FULL proof of 4.4, not merely its sequential consequence 4.8. For a Cartier W determined on pi, the condition Z<W for nef Weil Z is checked on finitely many pi-prime coefficients: BFJ 2.4 gives Z<=Z_pi on any refinement. Strict positivity of W_pi-Z_pi on the entire exceptional fibre pulls to strict positivity at every further exceptional valuation, so the finite inequalities imply the full strict inequalities. This set is open in the coefficient topology.

If the tuple's intersection is zero, upper semicontinuity is automatic because all intersections are <=0. At a negative intersection value it suffices to check thresholds t<0 above that value; positive thresholds are automatic. Choose nef Cartier majorants W_i whose intersection is <t using Definition 4.3. No W_i can then be zero, since that would give intersection zero. Their coefficients are strictly negative, by 2.4. Replacing them with (1-epsilon)W_i, with epsilon>0 sufficiently small, keeps their finite Cartier intersection <t and makes each inequality Z_i<W_i strict. The finite-determination open neighborhoods just described give intersection <t nearby. In particular a zero entry is covered by the automatic zero-value case. This reconstructs the upper semicontinuity argument of 4.4 in the actual coefficient topology.

For an arbitrary decreasing coefficient net Z_(i,lambda) -> Z_i, monotonicity gives each intersection >=the limit intersection, while upper semicontinuity gives limsup<=that limit. Therefore the intersections converge for ANY such net, with no countable-cofinality hypothesis. Apply this to the fixed negative ideal Cartier test Z(J) and the decreasing representations of the bounded inputs. After changing sign, BFJ's moments converge to precisely n3's scalar moment limits. The common mass bound and lattice density identify all Radon measures on ALL semivaluations. This establishes exact smooth OPERATOR specialization.

BFJ Remark 4.5 says multiplier approximation is essential for its additive Weil intersection. This is retained as a smooth published dependency, along with resolution and the Rees/Ramanujam Cartier comparison. It is not used to prove the singular kernel, geometry or locality. Other primary gauges use our proved (GAUGE), not an unstated BFJ theorem. Smooth DVR and dimension-zero cases are the direct n7 cases.

The exact one-factor gauge rule, reference mass, finite normalization with all residue degrees, full conductor quotient behavior, lower-top-degree zero, curve Cartier comparison, all degenerate cases and exact published smooth operator are proved.

There is no retained mathematical gap in the exact P12.4 target relative to the qualified G331 model system and reduction convention. The family explicitly separates cone, envelopes, bounded products, energy and general finite-map compatibility.
